title: Who can do what, and why?
summary: Login, ownership, private storage, service identity and security testing along the actual trust path.
opening_answer: Media owns authentication. API Gateway gets a trusted actor from Media’s authorizer, and each service checks it against its own records. Video objects stay private, with narrow temporary grants. Cloud roles are separate; scanners check specific boundaries and do not prove the system secure.

sections.title: Knowing who you are is only the first check

blocks.text: Authentication asks “who is calling?”; authorization asks “may they do this to this resource?” Arun can be logged in and still have no right to read Maya’s job.

Media hashes passwords with bcrypt and issues a signed JSON Web Token in an `access_token` cookie: Secure (HTTPS only), HttpOnly (hidden from page JavaScript), SameSite=Strict. These reduce risk but do not replace authorization.
The Media authorizer verifies the token and current user. Processing receives only the actor, not the signing secret or users table, and checks ownership of its own jobs.

blocks.q: Is authentication enough to stop one user reading another’s video?
blocks.a: No. Every protected operation also needs an ownership check; Arun is still denied Maya’s asset.

sections.title: The client cannot choose its own identity

spec.title: From a cookie to an owned operation

steps.label: Browser session
steps.detail: Supplying an x-owner-id header does not choose an owner.

steps.label: Media authorizer
steps.detail: Verifies token and current account; returns a structured Actor.

steps.label: Gateway adapter
steps.detail: Reads authorizer context only; strips caller-supplied identity headers.

steps.label: Owner check
steps.detail: Checks the actor against the service’s own resource records.

spec.caption: The integration marker is a schema fence, not a secret; AWS invocation policy is part of the boundary.

blocks.text: The adapter rejects missing or malformed context and ignores `x-owner-id` and `x-role`. Authorizer cache TTL is zero, so each decision uses the current account. Direct Lambda invocation with forged events must also be impossible.

blocks.q: Why not share the JWT secret with Processing?
blocks.a: Media owns identity. A trusted actor lets Processing enforce ownership without copying users or holding the secret. Tradeoff: depends on the Media authorizer.

blocks.q: What stops someone sending x-owner-id with another user’s ID?
blocks.a: The adapter strips caller-supplied identity headers and uses authorizer context; services compare that actor with the resource owner.

sections.title: Temporary access is not a public bucket

blocks.text: Upload uses a presigned POST with server-chosen key and policy fields on a bucket that rejects anonymous access; Media verifies the object before adopting it. The app cookie never reaches storage.
Playback: an owner-authorized request to Media returns short-lived output access. A signed URL is a capability for anyone holding it; keep it out of logs, screenshots and slides.
HLS needs a playlist plus segments (output namespaces validated); HLS is best effort, MP4 the fallback. Authenticated responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

blocks.q: Does private storage mean a browser never reaches an S3 public endpoint?
blocks.a: No. Privacy is an authorization policy; a signed operation can permit temporary access via S3’s public endpoint. Policy and network placement differ.

sections.title: A user session and an AWS role solve different problems

rows: Which AWS actions may a handler perform?
What may running worker code do?
Read sources, write outputs, consume work.
What may ECS do to start the container?
Pull images, set up logging, inject secrets.
May this workflow get short-lived AWS credentials?

blocks.text: Media and Processing have separate databases, logins and migrations, and since AD-29 separate Aurora clusters (`media_db` original, `processing_db` clone): physical failure isolation.
Schema validation is not producer authentication: `contracts/v1.py` rejects malformed envelopes, secrets and URLs; IAM and queue policies decide who may send.

blocks.q: What is the difference between an ECS task role and execution role?
blocks.a: The execution role lets ECS start the task (image pulls, secrets); the task role gives running code its AWS permissions. Neither is a user login.

sections.title: Security scanning feeds one place, and none of it proves safety

steps.label: Scanners
steps.detail: CodeQL (Python, JS/TS, Actions), Trivy per image, authenticated OWASP ZAP, Ruff security rules (Bandit), gitleaks.

steps.label: SARIF upload
steps.detail: Each tool publishes to GitHub code scanning. ZAP is report-only.

steps.label: Security tab
steps.detail: All scanners plus Dependabot alerts; secret scanning and push protection on.

steps.label: Triage
steps.detail: Fix, dismiss with a recorded reason, or accept unfixed with a receipt.

rows: All in test, proof or developer-script code, none deployed; dismissed with reasons
ZAP low/info on OpenAPI doc pages only
Accepted unfixed: no Debian 13 fix; finite worker, no inbound network

blocks.text: Also owner and malformed-identity tests and earlier AWS negative checks; none substitutes for another.
Image gate: zero fixable HIGH/CRITICAL; unfixed rows remain. SonarCloud NOT_RUN. DAST: seven GET routes of 20 operations, local harness only.

blocks.title: Answer pattern
blocks.text: Threat, control, test, remaining boundary: forged owner header; adapter ignores it; negative tests cover it; Lambda invocation policy is separate.

blocks.q: Is the system vulnerability-free because CI is green?
blocks.a: No. Green CI means the required checks passed for one source and scope; unfixed findings, DAST exclusions and unconfigured SonarCloud remain.

sources.label: Scanner set, SARIF upload and triage

takeaways: Authentication and ownership are separate checks.
Trace a trusted actor from Media’s authorizer into a service-owned operation.
Private buckets still use temporary signed access.
Separate app sessions, task roles, execution roles and deployment identity.
Scanners feed the Security tab; state what each proves.
